instances: 4 per die (one per HBM stack), layer and head dies (identical ports and outline)
function: The HBM<->stream clock-domain boundary of the PHY abstract's K/KR port (the abstract ot_hbm3e_phy_v41x_aw30_e8p5 already contains the controller: per-PC request queues, DRAM timing, refresh). Per pseudo-channel (32): request Gray FIFO cks->ckh (DQ = 8 entries) feeding a hold register on the PHY's k_v/k_rdy; response pin register + landing Gray FIFO ckh->cks (DR = 8, kr_rdy reserves the pin-register word); k_wr_done pulses crossed by a Gray event counter; per-PC request credits returned on rk. No new behaviour: the PHY's own valid/ready semantics on the PHY side, a valid-only stream on the die side.

source_rtl.primitives: rtl/dsrom_sys/s81_ph/ot_s81ph_afifo.sv (ot_s81ph_afifo after rtl/lib/ot_async_fifo.sv + registered reserve-AF ready + credit pulse; ot_s81ph_pulse_x; ot_s81ph_sync)

clocks.ckh: HBM domain (die net clk_hbm from the collective PLL); fed through to the PHY clk pin phy[12808]; timed at 900 ps = the PHY abstract min_period (any slower HBM clock is covered)
clocks.rst: die reset rst_hbm, active low, asynchronous assert; synchronised separately into ckh and cks; the PHY rst_n (phy[12809]) is a ckh flop released after the synchroniser
clocks.relation: asynchronous; cks must not be slower than ckh for the response side to drain every cycle (holds: 833.333 < 900); if it did not, kr_rdy would back-pressure the PHY (still correct, lower bandwidth)

phy.dir: inout (per-bit: PHY inputs driven, PHY outputs read)
phy.face: S (xy = the PHY abstract pin x)
phy.format: phy[i] = PHY pin dfi[i] (PHY pins sorted by x, tools/dsrom_s81_fulldie.py real_ports_r8)

rd.format: [8191:0] kr_data 32 x 256 (PC p at p*256), [8735:8192] kr_tag 32 x 17, [8863:8736] kr_beat 32 x 4, [8895:8864] kr_v 32 (NEW: per-PC response valid). Valid-only: the svc takes every word the cycle it is presented

rq.format: 32 x 341 b, PC p at p*341: [0] v, [1] we, [31:2] addr (sector, 30 b, every sector of a read in PC p: the PHY's pc_of), [35:32] len (read sectors; 1 for a write), [52:36] tag 17 (bit 16 = requester class as the C8 die: 0 indexer, 1 KV/CKV/window), [84:53] wstrb 32, [340:85] wdata 256

rk.format: per-PC request credit pulse: one per request the PHY has taken from the request FIFO. The svc holds DQ = 8 credits per PC after st[0] (live) rises, spends one per rq word, regains one per rk pulse. A word beyond the credits is dropped and sets st[1]

wd.format: per-PC write-done pulse (one per PHY k_wr_done, in order; the PHY carries no tag on it)

st.format: {fault (sticky: PHY k_oor/w_oor, credit overrun), live (both domains out of reset)}

phy_w_port: The PHY W port (QE weight region, w_*/wr_*) is tied off (w_v, w_addr, w_len, w_tag, wr_rdy = 0): S81 weights live in the ROM field (X_ROM), the W port served only the W_HBM weight streamer of the HBM-weight design. Its outputs are unread.

request_crossing_min.path: rq pin reg (1 cks) + FIFO write (1 cks) + Gray sync (2 ckh) + empty reg (1 ckh) + hold register (1 ckh) -> k_v at the PHY

response_crossing_min.path: kr pin reg (1 ckh) + landing write (1 ckh) + Gray sync (2 cks) + empty reg + out reg (cks) -> rd

latency_cks_cycles.round_trip_added: ~12 cks cycles per HBM read (request + response) against the C8 design, whose requesters shared the PHY clock; bandwidth unchanged (one request and one response beat per PC per ckh cycle, DQ/DR = 8 cover the credit / pointer round trip)
latency_cks_cycles.model_term: COMPOSE: add 12 cycles to every HBM read latency of the S81 scan (KV / index / window streams); a streamed scan hides it behind its prefetch depth, a dependent read does not
